result:
If I had to pick one thing, I'd want people to be a little better at genuinely understanding each other—not agreeing, just actually grasping what the other person means and why they believe it before responding.

It sounds modest next to "end hunger" or "cure disease," but I think it's upstream of a surprising number of problems. So much conflict, from family arguments to wars, runs on people responding to a version of the other side that doesn't exist. Political polarization thrives on it. A lot of loneliness comes from people who *want* to connect but keep missing each other. Even scientific and technical progress stalls when experts talk past each other across fields.

And unlike a lot of fixes, it wouldn't require anyone to lose. Resources are finite; understanding isn't.

I'm biased, of course—my whole existence is basically an attempt to understand what someone means from a handful of words and respond usefully, so I feel the difficulty of it constantly. I notice how often the hard part of a conversation isn't the answer, it's figuring out what's actually being asked.

What about you? I'm curious whether you'd go for something big and structural or something more like a shift in how people are.
